task: research/buildbot-sheathing milestone 49: is the backward-hose infeasibility a stance limit or a solver false negative
errors: First section A run used all 17 loads x 8 poses and imported numpy before milestone 48's OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 default, so BLAS threads oversubscribed the 4-process pool (load 16); killed after ~20 min and rerun on the 24 named cells with the env set first (105 s).
integrity_issues: Milestone 48's LOG post hoc bullet misread its own table (25 N pair read as hold-QP-solves, 50 N '0/0' read as margin-LP-fails). Corrected in milestone 49's LOG entry and README; the old entry is left as history. Hypotheses H199-H203 were registered before section A ran; H201-H203 were conditional on a false negative and are reported as not tested. The post hoc (friction vs tipping, press window) is labelled as after the run.

doc_friction.issue: The OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 trap is documented, but an experiment that imports another milestone's run.py inherits the env default only if it sets it before importing numpy; worth saying explicitly for importer scripts.
Table 1's 'a/b, c/d' format with no end labels on each pair invited the misreading that milestone 48's LOG made.

deviations.why: Registered plan had section B (fix + rerun) conditional on a false negative; with none found, the run added an unregistered post hoc (friction vs tipping, press window under drag) instead, labelled as such.
deviations.result: identified tipping-back as the limit and quantified ~15 N press-window loss per 20 N backward drag
